sources.note: The builder publishes no I, J, P or E, no STIX and no handicap number.

sources.what: The builder's longitudinal section with a 0–2 m scale bar, measured for the mast, the forestay's tack, the boom band, the keel and the rudder
sources.cite: Hallberg-Rassy, HR 40C interior side view (1900 × 858 px)
sources.note: 134.0 px/m by the scale bar. Checks: hull length 12.30 m (12.30 published); the waterline, not drawn, is placed 1.92 m above the keel's bottom and then reads 11.56 m long against 11.74 (−1.5%). Read off it: forestay tack 0.31 m aft of the stemhead; mast front 4.89 (a rendering in the brochure reads 4.85); boom band 5.34 m aft of the mast's aft face; keel at the hull 4.91–6.95 m, 1.59 m long above the bulb, 1.26 m deep, leading edge swept about 27°, the bulb 1.78 m long; rudder root 11.63 m, chords 0.45 and 0.19, span 1.18 (one of two canted blades, in projection). Fore and aft ±0.04 m; heights ±0.06 m. I (17.5 m) and P (16.3 m) are scaled off the brochure's perspective rendering, corrected by the published air draft: ±0.5 m.

published.note: Hull, weights, sail areas, the VPP and the stability curve are the builder's. Nothing about the rig's geometry is published: every rig dimension and every fore-and-aft position is read off the builder's section (I and P off a rendering). She is here for the VPP and the stability curve; her balance reading carries the least weight of the fleet.

vpp.what: Frers' VPP condition: sailing displacement 11.6 t (the crew is taken to be in it), sitting

polar.note: The designer's VPP, not measured speeds: a check that two VPPs agree. Its true wind is at the masthead (19.75 m), the tool's at its own reference height. Downwind is with the A2 and is not compared.

pinned.why: beat VMG 10–13% over Frers' VPP at every wind (she points 4–6° higher at 12 and 16 kn); reaching within 7%. Her I and P are ±0.5 m estimates, and Frers' wind is at the masthead.

mastAftOfStem.how: read off the builder's section by its scale bar; a rendering reads 4.85

keelLeAftOfStem.how: the same section; the root includes the deep-bilge sump

wlFwdAftOfStem.how: the same section, the waterline placed from the draft (±0.2 m)

balance.why: I, J, P, E, BAS, the mast, the forestay's tack, the keel and the rudder are all estimates (20 of the fields the balance reads); I and P are ±0.5 m off a rendering. She has twin canted rudders, modelled as one blade in projection, and a keel whose root is a hull sump. The synthetic hull also puts her waterline's forward end 0.34 m aft of the stem where the drawing's is nearly plumb.

disagreements.used: the VPP's, which the polar is compared with

published.estimatedWhy: BWL is 0.86 of the beam, a proportion: nothing gives it, and the stability comparison hangs on it. Tc, freeboard and every rig and appendage dimension are read off the builder's section; I and P off a rendering. The keel's section is the one that makes 3,650 kg of lead on the drawn planform (its bulb is folded into the fin). The rudder is one of two.
